text:
Anna L.: heads up — just saw strange authz in prod: a customer embedding key called /v1/chat/completions and succeeded. :eyes:
Kevin W.: whoa. can you paste the log lines?
Anna L.: log snippet:
```
[2026-04-02T13:04:12Z] api=embed-request route=/v1/chat/completions api_key=emb-* user_id=acct_123 status=200 model=gpt-open-13b scope=embeddings
```
Kevin W.: that suggests scope enforcement treated embeddings tokens as valid for chat endpoint. did we deploy the RBAC refactor earlier?
Maria G.: we merged rbac/v2 simplified-scope-checks at 12:45 — it replaced per-route allowlists with a normalized scope predicate.
Jack S.: SecBot alerted about KMS rotate job at 12:50 too. maybe cache invalidation edge-case? :thinking_face:
SecBot: ALERT: Key rotation job completed for KMS key ring proj-redwood-1 at 2026-04-02T12:50Z. Linked tokens may have stale metadata until KMS-metadata-cache TTL refresh.
Anna L.: hypothesis: during rotation we fall back to token metadata from auth-cache which lacks per-route scope flags, and the new predicate accidentally treats missing fields as permissive.
Kevin W.: if true, that means an allow-by-default bug when scope field is absent. can someone run an ad-hoc audit query for requests with api_key prefix "emb-" hitting chat routes in the 12:45-13:10 window?
Maria G.: running now: SQL:
```
SELECT timestamp, route, api_key_prefix, status
FROM access_logs
WHERE api_key_prefix = 'emb-' AND route LIKE '/v1/chat/%' AND timestamp BETWEEN '2026-04-02T12:40:00Z' AND '2026-04-02T13:15:00Z';
```
Maria G.: results: 42 hits, 37 successful 200s. correlated with KMS rotate and RBAC deploy.
Jack S.: immediate mitigation: revoke the implicated embedding keys and force rotation for affected customers? that's noisy. alternative: hotfix the auth service to treat missing scope as deny. less customer impact.
Anna L.: agreed. can we push deny-by-default hotfix to prod quickly?
Oliver R.: I'll open a small PR to add a defensive check: if token_metadata.scopes is null -> reject. also add unit test for KMS TTL path. plan to cut a hotfix branch now.
Kevin W.: also need an audit trail for which tokens were allowed — capture request ids and dump to protected S3 for incident review. Jack, can you own that?
Jack S.: on it. will run backfill for the 42 hits and upload.
Maria G.: note for postmortem: KMS rotation job sets metadata update but our metadata cache suffers a race where during refresh we expose a short window of default-constructed metadata. The RBAC refactor used truthy-checks (if scopes) which passed for empty object. fix is both code change + better schema validation on cache deserialization.
Anna L.: thumbs. also we should consider forcing KMS rotation to invalidate auth-cache keys immediately. Ops, is that feasible?
Kevin W.: yes, but needs coordination. Short-term hotfix first. Longer-term: atomic rotation + cache-invalidate step in KMS job.
SecBot: NOTE: I've created incident ticket INC-2026-0452 and set severity P2. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-0452
Oliver R.: PR opened: github.com/redwood/security/+/branches/hotfix-authz-missing-scopes. Patch adds null-check, explicit deny, and extra logging for scope source (kvs-cache vs kms). Requesting review from @Kevin W.
Kevin W.: reviewing now. quick testing steps: 1) deploy hotfix to canary, 2) replay a saved embedding token request against chat route, 3) confirm 403. please include exact curl for replay.
Oliver R.: curl for replay:
```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions" -H "Authorization: Bearer emb-testfake" -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}],"model":"gpt-open-13b"}' -v
```
Anna L.: once canary looks good, coordinate a fast rollback window if anything unexpected. notify support to expect customer key revocation messages if we revoke.
Jack S.: audit dump uploaded to secure S3 path s3://redwood-incident/INC-2026-0452/emb-chat-2026-04-02.csv
Maria G.: postmortem actions I'm adding to ticket: 1) schema validation on cache deserialize, 2) RBAC predicate unit tests for absent fields, 3) KMS rotation step to trigger cache invalidation, 4) add synthetic tests that run during deploy (inject fake rotate + auth checks).
Anna L.: thanks team. let's keep thread for updates. :white_check_mark:
Kevin W.: update: hotfix merged and deployed to canary at 13:30. monitoring for rejects.
SecBot: MONITORING: 13:35-13:45 canary observed 0 hits of emb-* -> chat accepted. rejecting as expected.
Oliver R.: will promote to prod at 13:50 after 15m canary.
Anna L.: after prod deploy, let's run an explicit audit and let affected customers know if we revoked or rotated their keys.
Kevin W.: will draft customer-facing blurb for support. keep confidential until notify list is ready.
